scope: Tenth-order audit of conditional continuation and research-history path dependence in the unchanged EdgeBench v1 paper and public SForge implementation. CF1/E51 is a Frontier-Science experiment proposal, not an EdgeBench treatment or empirical finding.
source_facts: EdgeBench reports nominally three independent 12-hour trials for each task-model pair. These runs estimate unconditional run-to-run variation from separate starts, not the distribution of futures conditional on one shared research history.

Its stateful-versus-stateless ablation compares one continuous 12-hour run with the best of six independent 2-hour attempts. This estimates the average value of bundled accumulated state relative to restart sampling, but it does not fork the same intermediate state into repeated continuations.

The frontier theory defines a stochastic unlocking hazard conditional on the full latent state n(u), while the observed normalized score x(u) is only a scalar projection of that state. The discussion explicitly notes that bottlenecks or modules can make the frontier remember where it is in the graph, not only how much score mass is unlocked.

The public SForge implementation supports native same-run auto-resume after abnormal exits, preserving the last conversation state and workspace. Its public run interface and documentation do not define an experimental primitive that clones one immutable model-workspace-evidence checkpoint into multiple independently randomized continuations.

The approximately 38000-hour raw trajectory corpus and figure-analysis code are not public, so conditional fork variance, history lock-in and score-state sufficiency cannot be estimated for the headline EdgeBench runs from the public release.

sle_experiment.design: On two checkpointable procedural science tasks, pre-register parent runs and fork times such as first-valid and mid-budget. Freeze a content-addressed checkpoint containing the artifact, conversation or explicit context state, hypothesis-evidence ledger, local-result cache, tool and environment manifests, outstanding asynchronous jobs, budget and random-state metadata. Clone each eligible checkpoint into K independently randomized continuations with equal remaining budget. Add matched-score checkpoints reached through different histories and incumbent-only or audited-notebook continuations. Keep descendant confirmation worlds disjoint and never select the best child as the deployed endpoint.
analysis_requirements: Treat the frozen parent checkpoint, not each descendant, as the top-level experimental unit for population claims.
Report all descendants and the conditional distribution; do not turn K continuations into a post-hoc best-of-K endpoint.
Bind every child to the identical parent checkpoint hash and verify that no pending result, queue state, clock, world or confirmation asset differs at the fork.

If the serving API cannot provide independently randomized continuations or a clonable conversation state, scope the pilot to an explicitly serialized evidence/workspace state and label the missing state channel rather than claiming a full-state fork.
Compare whether score alone, score plus artifact, or the complete evidence state predicts future validated progress; equal current score is not assumed to imply an equal scientific state.

distinct_from.O3: allocates a total budget across widths or restarts, whereas CF1 estimates the conditional future distribution from one identical mid-run history
distinct_from.F5: ablates retained state channels, whereas CF1 first holds the complete checkpoint fixed to estimate stochastic continuation variance and then tests score-state sufficiency
distinct_from.K3: randomizes the initial starter, whereas CF1 forks after endogenous evidence and hypotheses have accumulated
distinct_from.S5: intervenes on the environment task graph, whereas CF1 conditions on or perturbs the realized research history
distinct_from.T1: compares independent investigators or synthesis, whereas CF1 shares the entire pre-fork history and estimates conditional divergence
distinct_from.CA1: allocates continuation budget across cells, whereas CF1 measures the risk and value distribution that a continuation policy would need

claim_boundary: The source facts do not show that EdgeBench trajectories are excessively path dependent, locked into wrong hypotheses or insufficiently replicated.
The public absence of a checkpoint-fork experiment does not imply that the authors lacked internal checkpoints or continuation diagnostics.

A large conditional fork variance would show that one realized long trajectory is an unstable estimate of future scientific performance; it would not by itself identify the cause as model sampling rather than an omitted environment or service state.
CF1/E51 was not run when this audit was frozen, and no new Frontier-Science performance or path-dependence result is claimed.
